title: Python non-blocking structured event collector + iterator shim for streaming chat ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Teams integrating streaming chat completions need a low-friction Python surface that delivers structured events (tokens, tool-calls, function results, metadata) while avoiding blocking user code, supporting backpressure and cancellation, and making telemetry (latency, token costs, partial-output quality) straightforward. Current SDK patterns either expose raw SSE/text streams (too low-level) or synchronous blocking generators that make integration with async frameworks and long-running web servers clumsy.

Proposal: Implement a non-blocking StructuredEventCollector component plus a small async iterator shim for the Python SDK. The collector will: 1) accumulate and assemble partial events into typed artifacts (PartialText, ToolCallStart, ToolCallChunk, ToolCallEnd, FinalResponse, Error), 2) expose a safe async iterator that yields events as they become stable, 3) support explicit checkpoints for resume, and 4) surface developer signals for backpressure/cancel and cost telemetry. The iterator shim will provide both async (__aiter__) and sync (.sync_iter()) ergonomics via a lightweight thread-safe bridge to support sync-first apps.

API sketch: StructuredEventCollector(on_event: Callable[[Event], None], max_buffer_size: int = 1024, checkpoint_every: int = 50) -> CollectorHandle. CollectorHandle.async_iter() -> AsyncIterator[Event]; .sync_iter(timeout: Optional[float]) -> Iterator[Event]; .close(reason: str) to cancel and emit final Error event.

Key constraints: Must be non-blocking for event emission, avoid holding large token buffers in memory, keep kernel/quantization concerns separate (collector deals with semantic assembly only), and integrate with existing telemetry tags and token accounting.

Why unique: Focuses on the developer UX around structured events and the sync/async bridge rather than lower-level retry or resume internals documented elsewhere. Emphasizes typed events and telemetry hooks to make higher-level features (rollouts, quality monitoring) easier to implement downstream.
acceptance_criteria: Collector exists and can assemble at least: PartialText, ToolCallStart/Chunk/End, FinalResponse, and Error events
Async iterator yields events in order without blocking the HTTP streaming thread under typical workloads
Sync .sync_iter() provides correct semantics in sync callers and supports graceful cancellation
Unit tests for no-data idle periods, high-throughput partial chunks, cancellation and resume checkpointing
Integration test that wires collector into chat-completions endpoint and verifies telemetry tags and token accounting
PR reviewed by SDK lead and approved by PM; design doc linked and basic docstring examples provided
notes: 03-02: Spike completed. Prototype collector implemented in py-sdk/prototypes/collector_spike.py. Observed contention when consumer stalled; added bounded queue + backpressure callback to alleviates memory growth.
03-04: Design review with PM (Rafael Ortega) — PM requested explicit function-call events to enable tool invocation observability and to make server-side fallbacks easier.

03-05: Trade-off: we considered returning fully-assembled message objects only (blocking until message end) vs streaming partial tokens. Chose partial-first with typed events to support low-latency UIs and intermediate function-calls.
03-06: Security note: collector does not deserialize arbitrary user-provided code; function-call payloads are treated as opaque JSON blobs until user code invokes handler. No KMS changes required.
03-08: Telemetry: emit event-level spans (collector.receive, collector.emit) and per-partial-token counters. Work with infra to tag with model, route, and request-id.
03-10: PR (#4092) opened. Initial review requested from @jen-ops and @lia-docs for docstrings and examples. Some nits on naming (CollectorHandle vs StreamHandle).
03-11: UX feedback from design: provide a convenience ChatEventAssembler that maps sequences of events into conversation turns for UI components. Added as sub-issue ENG-642903.

implementation_plan: 1) Add prototype collector module and unit tests (spike branch)
2) Implement production API in sdk/streaming/collector.py with async iterator and sync bridge
3) Add telemetry hooks and token accounting integration points
4) Write end-to-end integration test against chat-completions mock server
5) Docs: SDK page + examples (async consumer, sync web framework consumer) + design note
6) Release behind feature flag and invite early SDK users to opt-in for feedback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Backpressure overload can cause increased latency or OOM in edge cases. Mitigation: bounded queue + backpressure callback that invokes default flow-control (drop or slow-produce) and emits alert telemetry.
Risk: Sync bridge could deadlock under certain event ordering. Mitigation: thorough stress tests with GIL-aware patterns, use queue with timeouts and clear drain semantics on close.

Risk: Misaligned telemetry tags will make query-ing expensive. Mitigation: follow standard tagging conventions (model, route, customer_id, request_id) and add test that validates tags on emitted spans.

release_notes: Added StructuredEventCollector and iterator shim behind 'structured_streaming' feature flag. Provides typed streaming events and sync/async ergonomics. Initial release to beta customers for feedback.
